thread.title: Here Are 10 Chip Stocks Breaking Out, Hitting Highs Or Setting Up

author: ED CARSON
title: Here Are 10 Chip Stocks Breaking Out, Hitting Highs Or Setting Up
text:
The Nasdaq composite rallied solidly Tuesday while the S&P 500 index and Dow Jones industrial average rose slightly in large part because chip-related stocks were big winners. Applied Materials ( AMAT ) and Cree ( CREE ) cleared buy points, Intel ( INTC ) and Micron Technology ( MU ) hit new highs, and Lam Research ( LRCX ) announced big shareholder returns. Meanwhile, Apple ( AAPL ), a big buyer of semiconductors, carved a new buy point.
X These chip plays, along with several others that are in buy range or setting up, are outperforming the S&P 500 index, as shown by their relative strength lines . The RS line for the iShares PHLX Semiconductor ( SOXX ) ETF matched a record high.
Some of these breakouts are late-stage bases, such as with Applied Materials. Other stocks are extended, like Micron, while Dow component Intel didn't complete a proper base. But several chip stocks are worth watching.
Investors also should watch semiconductors because a healthy chip sector is a positive sign for a market rally. First, chips are a big part of market weightings, especially the Nasdaq. Chips also make up the guts of so many tech products, from the Apple iPhone to PCs to servers and many more. If chip stocks are doing well, that's a good sign for tech stocks and tech demand overall.
Apple Apple fell 0.1% to 176.67 in Tuesday's stock market trading . Apple has now completed a high handle, with the top of the handle slightly above the left side of a short, V-shaped cup base . That means that Apple's buy point has actually risen, from 180.20 to 180.71.
Apple's RS line, which was lagging badly for several months, rose significantly in February. It's edged lower in the last few sessions, but is still above the high of the left side of the consolidation.
Apple fell 0.9% to 175.03 in Wednesday trades.
Applied Materials, Cree Break Out Applied Materials, a chip equipment giant, shot up 4.1% to a record close of 59.99 on Tuesday, clearing a 58.83 double-bottom buy point after trying to break out briefly last week. (You could also view 59.10 as alternative entry from a newly formed handle.)
Volume was 36% above normal, but you'd like to see trading that's at least 40% to 50% higher than average on a breakout to confirm strong institutional buying.
Applied Materials' RS line is not quite at its late-November peak, but is definitely above where it was at the middle of the "W" in the double-bottom base.
Applied Materials fell 1% to close at 59.42 Wednesday.
Applied Materials is in a fifth-stage base. Fifth-stage bases are more likely to fail and less likely to deliver big gains than early-stage bases.
Cree, which makes chips for LED lighting, vaulted 9.7% to 41.76 Tuesday, blasting above a 40.34 buy point in volume that was 372% above normal. The RS line is hitting a new high. Cree cleared a second-stage base.
Cree rose 2.7% Wednesday to 42.89.
Intel Stock Hits A High Intel stock rose 1.9% to 50.71 on Tuesday in average volume, reaching a record 51.33 intraday. But the Dow Jones component had not yet consolidated for six weeks, the minimum for a cup base. Intel's stock chart has had a string of bad luck. But the RS line is hitting new highs.
Intel rose 1.2% to 51.32 Wednesday.
Micron Technology Powers On Micron stock jumped 3.3% to 53.74 on Tuesday, its best reading since late 2000. It was the third straight robust gain in above-average volume.
Micron cleared a 47.08 double-bottom buy point on Feb. 26 and topped a 49.99 alternative entry on Monday. Shares are now extended from either entry.
Micron rose 0.4% to close at 53.97 Wednesday.
Lam Research Hikes Dividend, Buyback Lam Research popped 4.65% to 207.94 on Tuesday, making good progress toward a 218.58 double-bottom buy point. Lam's RS line is well off the consolidation's high, but is already at the peak of the "W" buy-point zone. Lam's base is fourth stage, however.
Lam gained 1.8% to 211.74 Wednesday.
The chip equipment maker raised its quarterly dividend by 120% to $1.10 a share on Tuesday. It also added $2 billion to its buyback plan, bringing the total authorization to about $4 billion.
Other Chip Stocks To Watch Western Digital ( WDC ), which makes flash memory via its SanDisk acquisition as well as hard drives, rose 4.3% to 93.80 on Tuesday, clearing a 93.41 double-bottom buy point in volume that was 54% above normal. The RS line is lagging though. Western Digital is in a second-stage base.
Western Digital gained 1.6% to 95.27 Wednesday.
Skyworks Solutions ( SWKS ), an Apple iPhone supplier, edged up 0.3% to 111.85 on Tuesday, just below a 112.38 cup-with-handle buy point. The RS line is well of its highs, but is at its best levels since late November and above the handle's peak. Skyworks is in a first-stage base.
Skyworks lost 0.3% to 111.54. Wednesday.
Marvell Technology Group ( MRVL ) edged up 0.3% to 23.57 on Tuesday. Marvell has now completed a handle in its existing shallow double-bottom base. That slightly lowers the primary buy point, to 24.05, from the prior 24.31. The RS line is not far off highs.
Marvell added 0.5% to 23.69 Wednesday.
Chip equipment makers ASML ( ASML ) and Teradyne ( TER ) need a few more days to form proper cup bases. Their RS lines are already at highs. ASML would be a second-stage base. Teradyne is working on a third-stage pattern.
